This is an RCT comparing two different anaesthetic drug regimens (continuous vs intermittent fentanyl infusion with ketamine and droperidol). The study involves 40 patients undergoing surgery, not volunteers. It evaluates anaesthetic maintenance regimens which is within scope.

This is described as a 'prospective study' in 24 patients, not a randomized controlled trial. It analyzes pharmacodynamic interactions using a response surface model rather than comparing interventions. No randomization is mentioned.

This is a methodological study to identify EEG/AEP parameters that differentiate consciousness from unconsciousness. While it involves patients receiving anesthesia, there is no randomization of anaesthetic interventions - it's a diagnostic accuracy study.
This study was conducted in nine healthy volunteers, not surgical patients. Volunteer studies are explicitly excluded per the selection criteria.

This study used a two-phase design where patients were first studied without BIS monitoring, then in a second phase with BIS monitoring. This is not a randomized controlled trial - it's a before-after comparison without concurrent randomization.

While this is an RCT, it compares hemodynamic control agents (esmolol, nicardipine) rather than anaesthetic regimens or depth monitors. The primary anaesthetic (desflurane-N2O) was the same across all groups. The intervention is not an anaesthetic intervention per se.
This is an observational study reporting the incidence of awareness in 19,575 patients. There is no intervention or randomization - it's purely descriptive epidemiology.

This is a randomized prospective study comparing two anaesthetic regimens (propofol-remifentanil vs sevoflurane-N2O) in 42 patients undergoing surgery. It directly compares anaesthetic drug regimens for induction and maintenance.

This is a randomized multicenter study comparing closed-loop BIS-guided propofol titration vs manual control. It evaluates an anaesthetic depth monitor (BIS) for guiding anaesthetic delivery, which is within scope.
While this compares etomidate to thiopentone sodium as induction agents, the abstract does not clearly state that patients were randomized. The study design is not explicitly described as an RCT.
This is documentation for a statistical software package for conducting meta-analyses. It is not a clinical study and has no relevance to anaesthetic interventions.

This study compares the Narcotrend monitor (explicitly listed in the selection criteria) with BIS monitoring during propofol-remifentanil anaesthesia in 50 patients undergoing orthopaedic surgery. It evaluates anaesthetic depth monitors.

This is a prospective randomized study comparing three anaesthetic regimens (remifentanil+desflurane, remifentanil+sevoflurane, alfentanil+desflurane) in 45 patients. It directly compares anaesthetic drug regimens.

This is a randomized study with 60 patients divided into six groups receiving different anaesthetic techniques (varying MAC levels of isoflurane, with/without fentanyl, with/without lidocaine). It compares anaesthetic regimens.

This is a randomized study comparing propofol/epidural vs propofol/epidural/nitrous oxide in 88 patients. It compares anaesthetic regimens and specifically addresses postoperative awareness as an outcome.

This is a randomized study comparing 3% vs 4.5% desflurane in 50% N2O for caesarean section in 72 parturients, with BIS monitoring to assess anaesthetic depth. It compares anaesthetic regimens with the goal of preventing awareness.
This is a prospective observational case study interviewing 11,785 patients about awareness. There is no intervention or randomization - it's an observational incidence study.
This is a case series reporting 14 representative cases of awareness. It is not an RCT and does not test any intervention.

This study compares tramadol vs morphine administered at wound closure for postoperative analgesia. The intervention is not an anaesthetic regimen or depth monitor - it's a post-operative pain management intervention.
